name: Allesthesia
citation: Cabanac, M. (1971). Physiological role of pleasure. Science, 173(4002), 1103-1107.

constructs.description: The reversal of hedonic valence in response to persistent or repeated stimulation. A pleasurable stimulus becomes aversive when homeostatic need is satiated.
Pleasure is contingent on physiological departure from setpoint. Alleviation of need (hunger, cold, pain) produces strong positive affect proportional to deficit magnitude.

rejection_rationale: Single mechanism, not a theory family — belongs at T2 level. Allesthesia (pleasure from homeostatic correction) is a single mechanism within IC, not a family of domain-level phenomena with constructs. It is properly a T2 template contributing TO the Adaptive Thermal Comfort T1.5 theory, not a T1.5 theory itself.

provenance.predecessor: Homeostatic theory (Cannon, 1932); hedonic theories of motivation
provenance.historical_context: Cabanac showed that the pleasantness of a stimulus depends on internal state — cold water feels pleasant when overheated, unpleasant when cold. Extended to architecture: thermal pleasure varies with thermal deficit.
